articles.title: Trump administration says biggest changes coming to infant formula in nearly 30 years
articles.summary: HHS said it's the first major update to formula standards in nearly 30 years.
articles.body:
The Food and Drug Administration (FDA) announced on Thursday it is proposing a new rule that will update the nutrient requirements for infant formula.

The Department of Health and Human Services (HHS), which oversees the FDA, said in a press release that it would be the first major update to infant formula standards in nearly 30 years.

The proposed rule would update requirements for vitamin A, vitamin D, iodine and manganese as well as reaffirm existing requirements for chloride, potassium, selenium and sodium, the agencies said.

It would also change the units of measure for two nutrients and request public input on possible requirements for ingredients not currently required in infant formula but sometimes added by manufacturers, they noted.

The ingredients not currently required include arachidonic acid (ARA), docosahexaenoic acid (DHA), and L-carnitine. Some studies have suggested they contribute greatly to infant growth, brain development and health.

The agency said there will be additional phases looking at the remaining required nutrients, potential new nutrient requirements and carbohydrate sources.

The FDA said it will welcome public comment during its phases and, in the future, will issue one final rule to cover all the proposed changes.

The FDA also released new data on chemical contaminant testing for infant formula and found that most samples tested had "low or non-detectable levels of chemical contaminants."

"Parents deserve confidence in every bottle they feed their baby," HHS Secretary Robert F. Kennedy, Jr. said in a statement, in part. "We will hold infant formula manufacturers to rigorous scientific standards and put babies' health first."

Last year, the HHS and FDA announced they would review the nutrition quality of infant formula in the U.S.

The FDA said the review -- part of its "Operation Stork Speed" initiative -- would look at whether current nutrient requirements need to be updated, including whether additional nutrients need to be considered.

Under current law, the HHS secretary reviews the table of required nutrients every four years as appropriate.

The FDA currently specifies 30 nutrients that must be included in infant formulas. There are minimum amounts for all 30 nutrients and maximum amounts for 10 nutrients, according to the agency.

Among the nutrients currently required are protein and fat, as well as vitamins A, D, E, K, folic acid, iron, magnesium and zinc.

Last year, then-FDA commissioner Dr. Marty Makary discussed removing seed oils from infant formulas. Many commercial baby formulas contain seed or vegetable oils due to the essential fatty acids they provide.

"Generally, they're believed to be pro-inflammatory," Makary said of seed oils during an interview on "Fox & Friends" in June 2025. "We don't want babies with general body inflammation. Forty percent of our nation's kids have a chronic condition. Many of those are tied to inflammation and insulin resistance."

Doctors have previously told ABC News that seed oils are not pro-inflammatory and can help lower glucose levels, improve insulin sensitivity, reduce bad (LDL) cholesterol, reduce triglycerides and increase levels of positive (HDL) cholesterol.

ABC News' Katie Kindelan contributed to this report.

articles.title: How lone crusader put Congress on victory lap
articles.summary: Congress’ Abhijit Wanjarri retains Nagpur graduates’ MLC seat, Congress’ only win among 28 seats across 4 states as BJP-led NDA takes 16.
articles.body: NAGPUR: The headquarters of Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS) emerged as Congress’ sole winning ground in a round of Legislative Council elections that covered 28 graduates’ and teachers’ constituencies across Maharashtra, Uttar Pradesh, Bihar and Karnataka.Abhijit Wanjarri’s re-election from Nagpur’s graduates’ constituency gave the party its only victory in the four-state tally, though the wider results favoured the BJP-led NDA, which won 16 of the 28 seats, with BJP securing 13 on its own.For Congress, the fact that this lone victory happened in hometown of Union minister Nitin Gadkari and CM Devendra Fadnavis, gave the grand old party enough reason to cheer. BJP had appointed revenue minister Chandrashekhar Bawankule, as the poll in-charge.Wanjari defeated BJP candidate Sudhakar Kohale by 3,271 votes to retain the seat for a second consecutive term. He polled 67,231 votes against Kohale’s 63,960 after the counting process moved beyond first preferences. The result extended Congress’ tenure in a constituency long associated with the BJP and its predecessor, the Jan Sangh.Independent candidate Nitesh Karale, who contested after breaking away from NCP (Sharadchandra Pawar), emerged as a major third force, securing 24,249 votes by the second round. In the end, his second preference votes helped Wanjarri to scrape through in the intensely fierce battle, that lasted for almost two daysWanjarri’s support among teachers and educational networks also proved significant. He reportedly received backing from around 35 teachers’ organisations. His association with Nagpur University’s Senate and his links with educational institutions helped consolidate support among graduates and teachers across the division’s six districts.The win builds on Wanjarri’s 2020 victory, when he defeated BJP candidate Sandip Joshi by more than 18,000 votes, ending the party’s long hold on the seat. The constituency’s history stretches back to 1958, when Jan Sangh leader Bachhraj Vyas won it. Subsequent representatives included Shridhar Sohoni, Vishnu Deshpande, Ramjivan Chaudhary, Dr Motiram Lahane, Dr Pramila Tople, Gangadharrao Fadnavis, Nitin Gadkari and Anil Sole.Gangadharrao Fadnavis, the chief minister’s father, represented the seat in 1978 and 1984. Gadkari won it four times, in 1990, 1996, 2002 and 2008.Prime Minister Narendra Modi mocked Congress over its failure to win seats in the four states despite voting being conducted through ballot papers, a method the party has repeatedly advocated in its criticism of electronic voting machines. Wanjarri’s victory gives Congress a counterpoint, even as it remains shut out of the other MLC contests cited.The BJP’s setback also followed an internal dispute over its candidate. Former MLC Anil Sole, who represented the constituency from 2014 to 2020, entered the contest as an Independent after being denied the party ticket. His decision exposed discontent over the selection process. Sole criticised the move towards top-down candidate selection, saying party workers were no longer consulted as they had been earlier. Though Sole backed out of the campaign, he remained on the ballot paper as the withdrawal date had passed. Sole secured over 200 votes.For Congress, the victory was more about “where” it happened rather than absolute numbers. articles.title: Gareth Ward defends Michelin-star Ynyshir after food hygeine debacle
articles.summary: Chef Gareth Ward defends how he operates in documentary after Ynyshir got a one-star hygiene rating.
articles.body:
The chef at Wales' only two-Michelin-star restaurant has defended the way he operates his kitchen after the venue came under scrutiny over food hygiene standards.

While chasing a third Michelin star, Ynyshir was handed a one-star hygiene rating in February and told to improve due to concerns about raw and undercooked foods.

The news made global headlines and was a blow to Ward and his team, but in Apple TV's documentary series Knife Edge: Chasing Michelin Stars, Ward said Ynyshir was "an incredible place".

"There's nothing in there that's amateurish," he told the programme. "I run a spotless kitchen."

Ward, who co-owns the restaurant near Machynlleth in mid Wales, added the hygiene rating had hurt, "because we are only trying to be the best".

"Whether you're a cafe, or a pub, or a two-Michelin-star restaurant. We've all got the same rules," he told the eight-part second series of the show, which follows elite chefs and their teams.

"But we go above and beyond everything to make what we do safe."

Ynyshir was previously ordered to stop serving raw lobster after Ceredigion council found "significant hazards" were not properly identified.

The restaurant received its first Michelin star in 2014 and its second in 2022, becoming the first and only restaurant in Wales to hold two.

It missed out on a third star at the ceremony this year.

The 16-seat restaurant serves Japanese-inspired raw dishes as part of its nearly £500 a head 30-course tasting menu, and accused inspectors of not understanding its specialised procedures .

By August, the council had reinstated its five-star hygiene rating after it found the "business had addressed all matters identified during the original inspection".

But, for Ynyshir, the scrutiny was a major setback, and Ward shared his frustration in the documentary.

"I'm very proud of my whole team and my business, and what we've achieved," he said.

"It's obviously massive in the media, which anyone instantly jumps on and thinks it's about cleanliness," he said. "I run a spotless kitchen.

"When something like this happens you're a bit blown away."

Ward said the restaurant served a lot of raw food and did a lot of things "that aren't normal".

"We have done some things wrong, but we don't deserve everything [we were accused of]," he said.

He said the inspection left him feeling the weight of responsibility, with more than 30 members of staff and the business potentially at risk.

Management of food safety at Ynyshir was categorised by inspectors as needing major improvement, as was cleanliness and condition of facilities, while "hygienic food handling" was rated "generally satisfactory".

A dirty floor, inadequate hand-washing facilities in some areas and broken equipment posing a potential contamination risk were also identified in the inspectors' report.

Ynyshir responded at the time, saying the inspection "identified a small number of minor issues typical of a busy professional kitchen situated in the countryside of rural Wales" which had been "rectified immediately and in full".

It said biological testing, at "significant cost" to the restaurant, had "conclusively confirmed that our techniques are safe, compliant and appropriate".

It said at the time it was prepared to work constructively with the council but expected "an informed, consistent and fair assessment process that recognises the realities of modern, non-conventional restaurants".

When Ynyshir was reinspected, Ceredigion council said the "business had addressed all matters identified during the original inspection".

articles.title: Começa evacuação em Oleshky, na Ucrânia, durante trégua humanitária | G1
articles.standfirst: Cidade ucraniana no sul do país está dominada por tropas russas. Papa Leão XIV e primeira-dama dos EUA, Melania Trump, ajudaram a negociar cessar-fogo localizado em Oleshky para evacuação da população e entrada de ajuda humanitária.
articles.summary: Cidade ucraniana no sul do país está dominada por tropas russas. Papa Leão XIV e primeira-dama dos EUA, Melania Trump, ajudaram a negociar cessar-fogo localizado em Oleshky para evacuação da população e entrada de ajuda humanitária.
articles.body:
Imagem estática extraída de um vídeo de drone sem data, divulgado em 12 de setembro de 2026, mostra prédios destruídos em Oleshky , região de Kherson, Ucrânia controlada pela Rússia. — Foto: 34ª Brigada de Fuzileiros Navais "Borysfen"/Divulgação via Reuters

A evacuação de parte da população em Oleshky, no sul da Ucrânia e ocupada pela Rússia , e a distribuição de ajuda humanitária na cidade começaram nesta sexta-feira (30), afirmou uma autoridade de alto escalão do governo ucraniano.

O número de moradores que planejam deixar Oleshky em direção a territórios sob controle ucraniano ainda estava incerto até a última atualização desta reportagem, afirmou feira o primeiro-ministro ucraniano, Serhii Koretskyi. Anteriormente, ele havia falado em 527 pessoas, porém voltou atrás.

"Não há números exatos neste momento. A operação de resgate está em andamento, e os dados estão mudando", escreveu Koretskyi no Telegram.

Ao mesmo tempo, o governo russo de Vladimir Putin afirmou que parte da população de Oleshky que sinalizou intenção de evacuar a cidade quer ir para a Rússia, e não para outra parte da Ucrânia. O governo Zelensky não havia se manifestado sobre essa afirmação até a última atualização desta reportagem.

Moradores de Oleshky estavam embarcando gradualmente em comboios humanitários para serem evacuados tanto para a Rússia quanto para a Ucrânia, a comissária russa para os direitos humanos, Yana Lantratova, que representa o Kremlin na cidade durante a trégua humanitária.

"As pessoas que desejam viajar para a Federação Russa estão se reunindo aqui. Também há pessoas que desejam viajar para a Ucrânia. Todos terão a oportunidade de fazê-lo", afirmou.

Oleshky fica na margem leste do Rio Dnipro, na região de Kherson, em frente à cidade de mesmo nome, que está sob controle das forças ucranianas. Tropas russas controlam Oleshky desde os primeiros dias da invasão da Ucrânia, iniciada em fevereiro de 2022.

O cessar-fogo em Oleshky, que é localizado e não se aplica às demais regiões da Ucrânia, foi mediado pelo papa Leão XIV e pela primeira-dama dos EUA, Melania Trump. A trégua humanitária começou na terça-feira. O governo Trump afirmou que a trégua também se aplica a Kherson, cidade grande vizinha a Oleshky.

Duas pessoas morreram na cidade desde o início do cessar-fogo por terem pisado em minas posicionadas anteriormente pelas tropas russas na região. Ambos os países afirmam que o cessar-fogo, previsto para durar terminar na segunda-feira (2), está sendo respeitado.

articles.title: Coreia do Sul criminaliza uso de óculos inteligentes em provas | G1
articles.standfirst: A medida prevê aumentar de um para três anos o período de suspensão para quem for flagrado usando os dispositivos para trapacear; mudança deve valer já nos exames de 2027.
articles.summary: A Coreia do Sul vai criminalizar o uso de óculos inteligentes em exames e ampliar para três anos a suspensão de estudantes que tentarem fraudar o vestibular Suneung.
articles.body:
Um par de óculos inteligentes em exibição na loja de óculos Eyedaq em Seul. — Foto: JUNG YEON-JE/AFP

A Coreia do Sul vai abrir processos criminais e punir estudantes que usarem óculos inteligentes para colar nos exames nacionais de admissão universitária , explicou um funcionário do governo à AFP nesta sexta-feira (30).

A venda de óculos inteligentes, que permitem tirar fotos e vídeos, se comunicar com um assistente de inteligência artificial (IA), entre outras funcionalidades, está em alta.

Mas também crescem as preocupações com seu uso fraudulento, seja gravando pessoas sem seu consentimento ou trapaceando em provas .

O exame de admissão universitária na Coreia do Sul, o "Suneung", é conhecido por seu alto nível de exigência e é obrigatório para ingressar nas melhores universidades do país.

As autoridades planejam que as pessoas pegas usando esses dispositivos fiquem impedidas de refazer o exame de admissão por três anos. Atualmente, a penalidade é de um ano.

"Vamos acelerar o processo para que as mudanças sejam aplicadas já nas provas do ano que vem", explicou Lee Joon-hyuk, funcionário do Ministério da Educação.

A iniciativa é anunciada após três estudantes terem sido flagrados usando óculos inteligentes durante exames organizados por universidades de Seul.

articles.title: Capadócia: desabamento em 'chaminés de fada' mata 2 e deixa 5 feridos | G1
articles.standfirst: Rochas se desprenderam no "Museu a Céu Aberto" de Gorëme, principal ponto turístico da Capadócia. Por ano, mais de um milhão de pessoas visitam o local. Duas pessoas morreram e cinco ficaram feridas, de acordo com autoridades locais.
articles.summary: O desabamento ocorreu no Museu a Céu Aberto de Goreme após fortes chuvas; equipes de resgate buscam feridos entre os escombros da atração patrimônio da Unesco.
articles.body:
Um caminhão de bombeiros e ambulâncias após a queda de pedras de uma chaminé de fada na região da Capadócia, na Turquia. — Foto: Ihlas News Agency/Reuters

Duas pessoas morreram e outras cinco ficaram feridas após rochas de uma "chaminé de fada" (formação geológica vulcânica típica da região) caírem após fortes chuvas na popular região turística turca da Capadócia, na quinta-feira (29), de acordo com autoridades locais.

As rochas estavam no "Museu a Céu Aberto" (Open-Air Museum) de Gorëme, principal ponto turístico da região e Patrimônio da Unesco. Por ano, 1,18 milhão de pessoas visitam a atração, que reúne uma série de cavernas que serviram de refúgio para cristãos entre os séculos X e XII.

A Capadócia, destino turístico popular no centro da Turquia, é famosa pelas formações geológicas chamadas "chaminés de fada". Turistas sobrevoam as formações rochosas em balões e caminham entre as rochas.

O deslizamento de terra ocorreu devido às fortes chuvas por volta das 15h15 do horário local. Fragmentos de rocha se desprenderam das "chaminés" e caíram sobre pessoas na região do museu, disse o governador de Nevşehir, Huseyin Kok, a repórteres.

As nacionalidades dos mortos e feridos não foram imediatamente esclarecidas.

Pelas redes sociais, autoridades informaram que as equipes de resgate ainda estavam vasculhando os escombros no local.

articles.title: Assalto em Pombal: Suspeitos são presos após roubo de R$ 70 mil | G1
articles.standfirst: Dupla foi presa em cidades diferentes do Sertão da Paraíba. Polícia recuperou 26 relógios roubados e apreendeu armas e a motocicleta utilizada no crime.
articles.summary: Assalto em Pombal termina com dois suspeitos presos e 26 relógios recuperados pela polícia no Sertão da Paraíba após prejuízo estimado em R$ 70 mil na loja.
articles.body:
Dois homens suspeitos de assaltar uma loja de produtos importados em Pombal , no Sertão da Paraíba, foram presos durante buscas realizadas pela polícia na região. O crime aconteceu na tarde da quarta-feira (28), quando a dupla entrou no estabelecimento, ameaçou clientes e funcionários e levou mercadorias e pertences pessoais. O prejuízo estimado pelo proprietário foi de aproximadamente R$ 70 mil.

De acordo com as informações divulgadas pela polícia, os suspeitos foram identificados como Gabriel Figueiredo Lima e Adriano dos Santos Silva . Um deles foi preso em Aparecida e o outro, em Sousa .

Durante as diligências, os policiais recuperaram 26 relógios que haviam sido levados da loja. Também foram apreendidos dois revólveres calibre .32, com munições, e a motocicleta utilizada no assalto.

Segundo a investigação, após o crime, os suspeitos passaram por Aparecida, onde deixaram parte dos produtos roubados, e depois seguiram para Sousa. Uma mulher também foi identificada por, supostamente, ter dado apoio à dupla após a fuga.

O assalto foi registrado por câmeras de segurança. As imagens mostram os dois homens entrando no estabelecimento como se fossem clientes. Depois, eles anunciam o roubo, ameaçam as pessoas presentes e efetuam dois disparos.

Além das prisões e da recuperação dos produtos, a polícia informou que, durante as diligências, também apreendeu uma quantidade de drogas. Pessoas que, segundo a investigação, davam apoio aos suspeitos foram conduzidas à delegacia por suspeita de envolvimento com tráfico de drogas e receptação.

Suspeitos são flagrados assaltando loja de importados no Sertão da PB e causam prejuízo de cerca de R$ 70 mil — Foto: Reprodução / TV Cabo Branco

articles.title: Terra Santa registra 6 focos de incêndio em 24 horas e capacita servidores no combate ao fogo | G1
articles.standfirst: Município do oeste do Pará prepara brigada para atuar no combate ao fogo em meio ao cenário de queimadas e fumaça na região.
articles.summary: Município do oeste do Pará prepara brigada para atuar no combate ao fogo em meio ao cenário de queimadas e fumaça na região.
articles.body:
Focos de incêndios em Terra Santa — Foto: Painel do Fogo

Terra Santa, no oeste do Pará, registrou seis focos de incêndio de grandes proporções nas últimas 24 horas, de acordo com o Painel do Fogo. Em meio ao avanço das queimadas e à presença de fumaça na região, a prefeitura iniciou uma capacitação de servidores municipais para reforçar as ações de prevenção e combate a incêndios florestais.

A formação da Brigada Municipal de Combate a Incêndios Florestais começou na segunda-feira (24), na Escola José Picanço Bentes, em parceria com o 35º Grupamento de Bombeiro Militar (GBM) de Oriximiná.

O treinamento tem como objetivo preparar os servidores para atuar de forma organizada e segura em situações de incêndio, contribuindo para a proteção de vidas, do meio ambiente e do patrimônio público.

Durante as atividades práticas, os participantes fizeram uma marcha de 5 km até o local do treinamento e participaram de uma simulação de combate a incêndio florestal. Eles também receberam orientações sobre a preparação de aceiros, a organização do terreno para conter o avanço do fogo e o uso de equipamentos como bolsas costais e abafadores.

A capacitação é promovida pela Prefeitura de Terra Santa, por meio da Secretaria Municipal de Segurança Pública e Defesa Civil. As instruções foram conduzidas por militares do 35º GBM de Oriximiná, com apoio do coordenador da Defesa Civil municipal, Sávio Ribeiro.

A iniciativa busca ampliar a preparação das equipes locais para atuar em situações de emergência. O treinamento ocorre em um momento em que municípios do oeste do Pará enfrentam queimadas e fumaça, cenário que aumenta a preocupação com os impactos ambientais e os riscos à saúde da população.

articles.title: Brasileiros concorrem nas eleições dos EUA; saiba quem são | G1
articles.standfirst: Felipe, Priscila e Rita concorrem nas eleições regionais da Flórida e de Massachusetts. Dois deles buscam a reeleição.
articles.summary: Felipe, Priscila e Rita concorrem nas eleições regionais da Flórida e de Massachusetts. Dois deles buscam a reeleição.
articles.body:
As eleições de meio de mandato dos Estados Unidos , chamadas de midterms, acontecem na próxima terça-feira (3). Os americanos vão às urnas para escolher novos representantes para o Congresso e também para o Legislativo estadual.

Alguns brasileiros fazem parte dos candidatos que irão disputar a preferência dos americanos. Não há nenhum competindo por uma vaga nacional no Senado ou na Câmara dos Representantes, mas o g1 encontrou três que concorrem nas eleições regionais da Flórida e de Massachusetts. Veja quem são eles:

Felipe Sousa-Lazaballet — Foto: Divulgação

Onde disputa: Câmara dos Representantes da Flórida, Distrito 42 Partido: Democrata Adversária: Bonnie Jackson, republicana

ampliar a oferta de moradias acessíveis;

fortalecer o financiamento das escolas públicas;

melhorar o acesso aos serviços de saúde.

Depois de viver cerca de 15 anos em situação migratória irregular nos Estados Unidos, Felipe Sousa-Lazaballet, de 40 anos, se naturalizou americano em 2021. Agora, ele disputa uma vaga na Câmara dos Representantes da Flórida pelo Partido Democrata.

Se eleito, Lazaballet poderá se tornar o primeiro ex-beneficiário do DACA a integrar o Legislativo estadual americano.

👉 DACA foi um programa federal criado durante o governo de Barack Obama para oferecer proteção temporária contra a deportação a imigrantes de até 31 anos que haviam entrado nos EUA antes dos 16 . Os beneficiários também recebiam autorização para trabalhar legalmente no país.

Natural de Duque de Caxias, na Baixada Fluminense do Rio de Janeiro, e filho de mãe solo, uma empregada doméstica natural do Ceará, o brasileiro chegou ao país aos 14 anos e, aos 26 anos, através do DACA, recebeu permissão para trabalhar.

Em 2020, quando se casou com Luis Sousa-Lazaballet, Felipe já possuía o green card, obtido através de uma petição familiar. Em 2021, conquistou definitivamente a cidadania americana.

Ativista em organizações de defesa dos direitos dos imigrantes e da comunidade LGBTQ+ , ele também trabalhou cinco anos na administração do prefeito de Orlando, Buddy Dyer.

Em entrevista ao g1 , ele conta que vêm sendo atacado por sua adversária republicana pelo fato de ser imigrante e por estar há 10 anos na Flórida.

No entanto, entre os eleitores, ele sente que sua história de superação é vista de forma positiva:

"Cheguei nos EUA com 14 anos, literalmente com uma mala, um coração cheio de sonhos e nada mais. Foi justamente por causa desse processo tão difícil, de ser uma pessoa imigrante nesse país, que eu me envolvi com a política. Para ajudar as pessoas e buscar mudanças sociais. Minha história de superação indica que eu sei o que é sofrer e ter que lutar pelo sonho americano".

Priscila Sousa, brasileira que é representante do 6º distrito de Middlesex, Massachusetts — Foto: Kate Donaghue / Divulgação

Onde disputa: Câmara dos Representantes de Massachusetts, 6º Distrito de Middlesex Partido: Democrata

defende o aumento de recursos para escolas públicas e o suporte a estudantes imigrantes e de baixa renda;

expansão do acesso à saúde comunitária, saúde mental e a proteção legal aos direitos reprodutivos;

facilitar o diálogo do governo estadual com a expressiva comunidade brasileira e hispânica de seu distrito.

Nascida em Ipatinga, Minas Gerais, Priscila mudou-se para os Estados Unidos aos 7 anos e foi criada em Framingham, cidade que abriga uma das maiores e mais tradicionais comunidades brasileiras dos EUA . São cerca de 8 mil brasileiros em uma população de 72 mil habitantes.

Priscila obteve o green card no ano de 2004, aos 16 anos. Anos depois, formalizou sua situação e virou cidadã americana.

Em 2009, obteve seu diploma em Ciência Política, Relações Internacionais e Inglês pela Simmons University.

Este ano, Priscila, que tem 38 anos, concorre a sua segunda reeleição. Ela é a representante do 6º distrito de Middlesex desde janeiro de 2023 - os mandatos duram dois anos.

Questionada se já sofreu preconceito por ser imigrante, Priscila diz que sempre foi bem acolhida na Câmara de Vereadores e de Deputados do estado, mas que a situação mudou após a volta de Donald Trump à Presidência:

"Quanto à discriminação dos eleitores ou da comunidade em geral, nós vimos, infelizmente, acontecer mais depois da eleição do presidente Donald Trump. Certas ideologistas, mentalidades, certo desprezo ao estrangeiro imigrante... Mas continuamos lutando".

A lista eleitoral consultada mostra apenas o nome dela nessa disputa, portanto ela está praticamente garantida para um novo mandato.

➡️ Este tipo de disputa é chamada nos EUA de eleição sem oposição. Em distritos com forte inclinação política (onde um partido tradicionalmente ganha com mais de 70% dos votos), o partido de oposição muitas vezes prefere poupar recursos financeiros e não lança nenhum candidato, deixando a cadeira livre para o favorito.

Em 2017, Priscila concorreu ao cargo de prefeita de Framingham, mas terminou o primeiro turno da eleição em quarto lugar.

articles.title: Quatro homens são presos com drogas, arma e R$ 35 mil em Roraima | G1
articles.standfirst: Um dos locais alvo da ação tinha uma placa que dizia: “Lembre-se: maconha não mata, o que mata é não pagar o traficante". Prisões ocorreram nesta quarta (28).
articles.summary: Ação policial ocorreu em barbearia e casas nesta quarta-feira (28). Investigação começou após análise de transferências bancárias no celular de um suspeito.
articles.body:
Ficco-RR apreende drogas, dinheiro em espécie e pistola em Rorainópolis. — Foto: Divulgação/Ficco-RR

Quatro homens foram presos em flagrante por tráfico nesta quarta-feira (28) em Rorainópolis , na região Sul do estado. A prisão ocorreu após a polícia descobrir um esquema de venda de drogas na cidade. Durante a ação, os policiais apreenderam mais de 2,5 kg de drogas .

O material incluía cocaína , pasta-base e skunk . As equipes também encontraram R$ 35,6 mil em dinheiro, uma pistola calibre 9 milímetros e 30 munições . O grupo atuava em uma barbearia e em residências usadas para guardar os materiais.

Todo o dinheiro apreendido estava escondido em diferentes locais de um dos imóveis. No local, os policiais também acharam um cartaz com uma mensagem de ameaça a usuários com dívidas. O texto dizia: “Lembre-se: maconha não mata, o que mata é não pagar o traficante” .

As investigações começaram após a polícia analisar o celular de um investigado, com autorização da Justiça. As mensagens mostravam transferências bancárias relacionadas ao comércio ilícito. A partir disso, os agentes identificaram os fornecedores e os responsáveis por armazenar o material.

Os quatro homens foram levados para a Delegacia de Polícia Civil de Rorainópolis. Eles devem responder pelos crimes de tráfico de drogas e associação para o tráfico . Um deles também foi indiciado por posse ilegal de arma de fogo.

Placa encontrada em casa alvo de operação da Ficco-RR onde quatro foram presos por tráfico de drogas. — Foto: Divulgação/Ficco-RR

A operação foi realizada pela Força Integrada de Combate ao Crime Organizado em Roraima (Ficco-RR), que incluir as polícias Federal (PF), Civil (PC), Militar (PM) e Penal (PP) de Roraima. A atuação delas ocorre de forma conjunta no estado para o enfrentamento de organizações criminosas.

articles.title: Prefeitura de Rio Preto diz que vai manter projetos esportivos | G1
articles.standfirst: Gestão havia informado interrupção de aulas e dos pagamentos que beneficiam quase 300 profissionais e esportistas e atendem mais de 5 mil pessoas.
articles.summary: Projetos esportivos em Rio Preto seguem ativos após recuo da prefeitura, que ainda não confirmou a retomada do auxílio-atleta para cerca de 300 profissionais.
articles.body:
A Prefeitura de São José do Rio Preto (SP) voltou atrás e afirmou que não vai paralisar os projetos esportivos do município após anunciar a suspensão de atividades . A mudança de posicionamento foi divulgada na quinta-feira (29), depois da repercussão da medida. Contudo, o novo anúncio da prefeitura não informa sobre a retomada do pagamento do auxílio-atleta.

Na terça-feira (27), a administração municipal havia informado a suspensão das aulas de iniciação esportiva, das atividades destinadas a adultos e idosos, além da interrupção no pagamento de quase 300 auxílios a atletas, técnicos e professores.

Natalone promove aulas esportivas para pessoas com deficiência em Rio Preto (SP) — Foto: Prefeitura de Rio Preto/Divulgação

Segundo a prefeitura, a decisão estava relacionada à necessidade de adequações orçamentárias. Apesar da garantia de continuidade das atividades, a administração não esclareceu se os pagamentos do auxílio-atleta serão retomados ou mantidos.

O Auxílio ao Atleta e ao Técnico Desportivo Amador de São José do Rio Preto não é direcionado a alunos que apenas frequentam as aulas de iniciação esportiva, mas sim a atletas de competições e a técnicos/professores que ministram essas modalidades e treinamentos pelo município.

Os vereadores da Câmara estudam repassar para a prefeitura R$ 500 mil com o objetivo de custear os pagamentos. O dinheiro sairia de uma sobra do orçamento do Poder Legislativo. O envio da verba está sob análise, porque parlamentares aguardam um posicionamento sobre a necessidade da pasta.

O g1 questionou o vice-presidente da Câmara, Paulo Paulera ( PP ), sobre o repasse, mas não obteve retorno até a última atualização desta reportagem.

Também não informou se haverá remanejamento ou desligamento de profissionais envolvidos nos projetos . Em nota oficial, a gestão do prefeito Fábio Cândido ( PL ) afirmou que trabalha para garantir a continuidade.

“Não haverá paralisação dos projetos esportivos e a prefeitura está trabalhando para assegurar a continuidade das aulas e a valorização dos profissionais envolvidos”, diz a nota.

A administração destacou que os projetos atendem atualmente mais de cinco mil pessoas , entre crianças, adolescentes, adultos e idosos.

Ao g1 , a Secretaria de Esportes informou que a despesa média mensal com o auxílio-atleta entre janeiro e setembro de 2026 foi de R$ 667.761. O valor é 43% maior que a média mensal de R$ 465.812 registrada em 2025.

A prefeitura atribuiu a suspensão à necessidade de adequação orçamentária, mas não informou o valor total previsto no orçamento de 2026 para os programas.

Na folha de pagamento de outubro, 291 pessoas receberam valores relacionados ao programa, que somaram R$ 441.932,44. Os pagamentos individuais variaram de aproximadamente R$ 200 a R$ 3,3 mil, conforme a função desempenhada e a quantidade de horas dedicadas às atividades.

Sobre o planejamento dos pagamentos, a prefeitura informou que o programa previa repasses aos atletas de competição até outubro de 2026. Para os meses seguintes, a continuidade do auxílio estava direcionada principalmente aos profissionais responsáveis pelas aulas e atividades esportivas.

articles.title: MLC polls: Nitin Gadkari confidant revolt may’ve hit BJP in Nagpur
articles.summary: NAGPUR: Abhijit Wanjarri’s victory for a second consecutive term in the RSS citadel, home turf of Maharashtra CM Devendra Fadnavis and Union minister
articles.body: NAGPUR: Abhijit Wanjarri’s victory for a second consecutive term in the RSS citadel, home turf of Maharashtra CM Devendra Fadnavis and Union minister Nitin Gadkari, dealt BJP a major setback in its strongest political bastion and sharpened qu­estions over candidate selection. He defeated BJP’s Sudhakar Kohale by 3,271 votes.“I used brains against BJP’s might,” he said. He was the lone Congress nominee to win MLC polls held on Oct 23 that covered 28 graduate and teachers’ constituencies across Bihar, Karnataka, Maharashtra and UP.Former MLC Anil Sole, a Gadkari confidant denied a ticket, entered the contest as an Independent and stopped campaigning only after Fadnavis visited his home to resolve the dispute. The extent to which his rebellion hurt Kohale remains unclear.Over 15,000 votes were declared invalid in Nagpur, including nearly 9,000 ballots allegedly marked with the number ‘2’ against Kohale, but without preferences for the other 37 candidates. High count raised questions over voter error and discontent with candidate selection.Kohale said he would appeal against the invalid votes.Nagpur was a prestigious seat for BJP: Gadkari represented the graduates’ constituency from 1990 to 2014. Chandrashekhar Bawanku­le, who was in charge of the campaign, accepted responsibility for the defeat. “We will ensure we win the seat in the next polls,” he said.BJP contested three seats in Maharashtra but won only Pune graduates, where Kaustubh Gawade defeated Shiv Sena rebel Sachin Sanap. Sena had earlier backed rebels against BJP nominees in Pu­ne, where the allies clashed over seat-sharing. “We’ll tra­ck down who played spoilsp­ort. Corrective measures will be taken,” Bawankule said.A BJP member alleged that Sena workers campaigned against its candidate Smita Jadhav in Pune teachers, contributing to her defeat. “Had Mahayuti contested unitedly, we would have won all five seats,” they said.Sena hit back, with its Pune unit chief Ravindra Dhangekar saying BJP should stop taking alliance partners for granted. “The verdict has come as a reality check for BJP,” he said.Aurangabad graduates’ seat exposed another rift within Mahayuti, as NCP-SP’s Pratapsinh Patil defeated NCP nominee Satish Chavan.Sena veteran Abdul Sattar admitted backing Sharad Pawar’s candidate instead of his alliance partner’s nominee, blaming NCP’s choice of candidate. “This time, the candidate selection was wrong, so we did not campaign for him,” Sattar said, adding educated voters were moving away from the alliance.NCP failed to open its account. articles.title: Funds sought to recast slavery memorial sculptures in bronze
articles.summary: Sokari Douglas Camp has planning permission for the work in Southwark but needs money to recast the steel figures in bronze.
articles.body:
An artist with planning permission for a memorial to enslaved people in south London is trying to raise the money to make it permanent.

Sokari Douglas Camp's All the World is Now Richer is a set of six steel figures, which Southwark Council has approved for a site near Burgess Park.

To stand outdoors for the long term, the sculptures would need to be recast in bronze so the figures - and the words they carry - do not weather away.

The steel versions were on display at the Flowers Gallery to coincide with Black History Month.

Douglas Camp said the history of the work was "part of our heritage that people should know about", because it explained how England became the rich country it is.

She said she was inspired by William Prescott, a formerly enslaved man who said people would remember that they had been slaves, but not that they had been brave.

"Normally black people are seen cowering in some way or begging in some way," she said.

"We were strong. We were brave. We survived."

School pupils from Southwark who visited the sculptures said: "These might help you understand your background, your history and your ethnicity, and be proud of it."

Another said: "I think it's important because I'm black and it's really good to show our heritage."

Douglas Camp said the borough was home to many people from the Caribbean and across the African continent.

"We have a story to tell about how our people created wealth for this country," she said.

articles.title: AI makes Britain's largest woodland bat survey possible, scientists say
articles.summary: Some of Britain's rarest and most threatened bats have been recorded in the south-west of England.
articles.body:
Britain's largest ever woodland survey of bats would "simply not have been feasible" without AI, scientists say.

Researchers left devices on poles among the trees of 310 woodlands across Britain, recording 98 million bat calls over three years, which would have taken more than 30 years to analyse without AI.

Some of Britain's rarest and most threatened bats, including the red-listed Barbastelle, have been recorded in the south-west of England, including Somerset, Devon, Cornwall and Dorset.

Kate Jones, from University College London, said: "AI has fundamentally changed the scale at which we can monitor wildlife." She added the survey was a "nice story of AI for good".

Jones added: "Previously, analysing this volume of acoustic data would simply not have been feasible.

"These efficient open-source AI tools allow us to identify millions of bat calls across thousands of nights of recordings, identify patterns and flag species at a national scale."

The Barbastelle roams ancient forests but its elusive nature has made it challenging to track.

Hotspots of Barbastelle activity detected in the survey were concentrated across the South West.

Lia Gilmour, of the Bat Conservation Trust, which was involved in the survey alongside Forest Research, said the project was "unprecedented".

"We're getting some really good bat activity in the south-west area of Somerset," Gilmour said.

"Somerset is generally a really good stronghold for the bat species we have across the UK.

"It's been quite exciting some of the rarest species popping up in Somerset as part of the survey.

"In biodiversity monitoring, we view AI as a powerful tool," Gilmour added.

"We were looking at huge volumes of data and 90,000 hours of recording, there was no way we would be able to do this manually."

articles.title: University of Georgia secures $8 million NOAA grant to plan restoration of 326 acres of salt marsh across four states using dredged sediment
articles.summary: The University of Georgia has received an $8 million grant from NOAA Fisheries to lead a three-year initiative to restore salt marsh habitat along the
articles.body: The University of Georgia has received an $8 million grant from NOAA Fisheries to lead a three-year initiative to restore salt marsh habitat along the South Atlantic coast. The project will cover areas from North Carolina to Florida and will assess whether dredged sediment can help restore marshes threatened by rising sea levels, coastal development and pollution.The initiative was one of 16 habitat restoration projects selected from nearly 350 proposals submitted nationwide. It was proposed by UGA Marine Extension and Georgia Sea Grant through the South Atlantic Salt Marsh Initiative, a collaboration involving more than 300 partners. According to the University of Georgia, it could support restoration of 326 acres across four states.UGA received $8 million to plan salt marsh restoration across four statesThe University of Georgia will use the NOAA Fisheries grant to lead a three-year regional effort focused on salt marshes along the South Atlantic coast. The initiative will extend from North Carolina to Florida and bring together organisations working in each state. The project was one of 16 habitat restoration efforts selected by NOAA from nearly 350 proposals submitted across the United States.UGA Marine Extension and Georgia Sea Grant proposed the work through the South Atlantic Salt Marsh Initiative (SASMI). The collaboration includes more than 300 partners seeking to protect and restore marshes along the coastline. Georgia contains 368,000 acres of the nearly 1 million acres of salt marsh found across the region.How will dredged sediment help restore salt marshesThe project will assess whether sediment removed from navigational waterways can be used to restore nearby salt marshes. This material, known as dredged sediment, is usually placed in containment areas, dumped miles offshore, or used for beach nourishment.The UGA-led initiative will examine how dredged sediment can be kept within the coastal system and applied directly to nearby marshes. This would raise marsh elevation, allowing plants to grow and helping to improve the habitat. The project will assess the approach at proposed restoration sites across the four states and develop engineering designs for each location. These designs will guide the future implementation of the restoration work.Importance of salt marshes for coastal ecosystems and wildlifeSalt marshes face several pressures, including rising sea levels, coastal development, and pollution. Mark Risse, the project's primary investigator and director of UGA Marine Extension and Georgia Sea Grant, said, “Working through SASMI allows UGA to bring science and multistate coordination together to restore these critical coastal ecosystems across state lines”“Salt marshes serve as vital nursery grounds and habitat for fish and wildlife. They filter pollutants and protect communities from storms and flooding by buffering wave energy.”Which four sites could benefit from the salt marsh restoration projectThe initiative identified four proposed restoration sites: Bird-Long Island in Georgia, Cape Lookout National Seashore in North Carolina, Cape Romain National Wildlife Refuge in South Carolina, and Julia’s Island in Florida. At the end of the project, each state is expected to have engineering designs for its proposed site.Once implemented, the state-based projects have the potential to restore a total of 326 acres of salt marsh across the region. UGA and its partners also aim to develop standard restoration practices that use dredged sediment across multiple locations. articles.title: The Gloucestershire man who chooses to sleep with bedbugs
articles.summary: Dr Richard Naylor has about 50,000 bedbugs at his laboratory in the Forest of Dean.
articles.body:
A scientist has chosen to sleep with bedbugs for the past five years - and says the bites "don't bother him at all".

Entomologist Dr Richard Naylor breeds thousands of bedbugs to test pest control products from all over the world and allows himself to be the test subject.

On a "feeding day", which happens around twice a week, he straps some of his 50-60,000 bugs to his arm and gets on with his work. He then sleeps with them on nights when he needs to test out new devices or repellents.

"I must have been bitten millions of times by now, so I stopped reacting a long time ago. I get a red patch on my arm after the bugs have fed, but it disappears after about half an hour," he said.

Naylor explained that he needed to sleep with the bugs to test if new sprays and repellents worked.

"If there is no-one sleeping in a bed, the bedbugs just sleep, they just go on standby. And so I can't test anything in the test bedrooms without there being a host in there," he added.

GCHQ intern who took data home loses sentence appeal

'I was not living a normal life, I was surviving'

Home Guard training documents discovered in attic

Naylor runs a not-for-profit called the Bed Bug Foundation and has a research laboratory set up in a self-contained two-bedroom suite in his garden in the Forest of Dean, Gloucestershire.

He breeds the bugs and sends them all over the world, often to canine detection teams who help hotels spot infestations.

Naylor also uses the insects to help businesses test products before they come to market.

Bedbugs have become resistant to modern insecticide sprays, which makes them very difficult to kill and having an infestation can have long-lasting effects, according to Naylor.

"I don't know of any other pest that has the same level of emotional and psychological impact on people.

"It can leave people with lasting PTSD-type symptoms," he added.

Naylor said it could be difficult to deal with infestations and he advised anyone who suspected they had one to contact a professional.

"A key sign you have bedbugs is the inky black spots the bugs leave behind, often in the shape of an x.

"They don't hide in the bedding, they want to hide nearby in a little dark crevice. It would probably be somewhere down the back of the bed or around zips and the piping around the edge of a mattress," he said.

The Bed Bug Foundation gives the following advice to anyone who suspects they may have bad bugs:

Declutter around the bed (helps you to spot bedbugs that try to run away)

Remove bedding and other soft furnishings and put in bin bags for washing

Inspect the mattress and bed frame, especially near the head of the bed

Fit bed isolation devices to stop the bedbugs coming back

Ade Williams, lead pharmacist at Bedminster Pharmacy in Bristol, said bedbug bites tended to be clustered in a group, or be spread out in a line.

"Outside of the immense discomfort they cause by itching, they don't usually carry any health risks", he said.

However, Williams advised people to try not to itch bites as they could become infected, and said antihistamine tablets and emollient creams could help.

It advises putting something cool, like a clean, damp cloth, on the affected area to help with the itching and any swelling and to keep the affected area clean.

articles.summary: Israel is facing weeks, and possibly months, of political uncertainty after the final election results showed that neither Prime Minister Benjamin
articles.body: Israel is facing weeks, and possibly months, of political uncertainty after the final election results showed that neither Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's bloc nor the opposition secured the 61 seats needed to form a government.The results have left the country with a hung parliament, with Arab-led parties potentially holding the key to the next government.According to CNN, the results released by election officials early Friday showed Netanyahu's right-wing bloc winning 53 seats in the 120-member Knesset, while the opposition, led by centrist Yashar party leader Gadi Eisenkot, secured 48 seats. Arab-led parties won the remaining 19 seats.The opposition has accused the longest-serving PM Netanyahu of targeting the Arab population and attempting to undermine the election's credibility after the historic performance by Arab-led parties.If the opposition joins hands with the Arab parties, it could potentially secure a parliamentary majority. However, he is not expected to give up his alliance with far-right Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich and the ultra-Orthodox parties.Eisenkot, however, has ruled out joining a government led by Netanyahu. Any change in that position could also anger voters who want to see Netanyahu leave office.3. Netanyahu forms govt with oppn defectorsNetanyahu could also try to attract lawmakers from opposition parties to secure the numbers needed to form a government.However, all four opposition leaders, Eisenkot, Bennett, Liberman and Yair Golan, have ruled out joining a government led by him.With Netanyahu's bloc eight seats short of a majority, he would need to persuade at least eight opposition lawmakers to switch sides. articles.title: Survivors of Spain’s worst train crashes urge action after latest disaster
articles.summary: As people suffering post-traumatic stress watch history repeat itself, experts call for investment in safety.
articles.body:
Madrid, Spain – “I survived but the mental scars are still there all these years later. We must stop more accidents happening,” says Cristobal Gonalez.

Gonzalez suffered multiple injuries when a high-speed train, which should have been travelling at 80 kilometres per hour (50 miles per hour), hurtled off the line at 200km/h (125mph), killing 80 people.

The accident in 2013 at Angrois, near Santiago de Compostela in northwestern Spain, remains Spain’s deadliest rail crash.

On Wednesday, 13 years later, at least 69 people were killed when two trains collided near Urda, a town close to Toledo in central Spain. Only 10 months earlier, two other trains collided on the same line, in Adamuz near Cordoba in southern Spain, killing 46 people.

Survivors of Spain’s three worst rail disasters have said more must be done to avoid further tragedies.

“Now we have seen three dreadful crashes in Spain, at Angrois, Adamuz and Urda. They will keep happening if we do not act,” Gonzalez told Al Jazeera.

“At Angrois, the driver was going too fast; at Adamuz, an investigation said there was a problem on the track; and at Urda it might have been human error and a problem with the control system. Whatever, we must stop these crashes happening by investing more in safety.”

Gonzalez was travelling with a friend, Oscar, to Santiago de Compostela when the crash happened. He was in the front carriage when the train “flew” off the tracks and smashed into a bank.

He stayed inside the train trying to help others in their last moments. Years later, he struggles to talk about the events of that day.

“I will keep what happened to myself. It is very hard to share it, even if I wanted to – it is something that defies imagination,” said Gonzalez, who suffers from post-traumatic stress.

‘I cannot believe that this has happened again’

Santiago Rosendo, who was one of the passengers in the Renfe train involved in the Adamuz crash in January, spoke of the “panic” among passengers when the trains collided.

“There was a sudden stop – a very sudden stop – then following that, a loud crash. Then the train moved from side to side until the train slid onto its side and we were left entirely in the dark. The first thing I saw when I got off the train was a body,” he told Al Jazeera.

Rosendo, who was travelling on his own from Madrid to Huelva in southern Spain when the accident happened on a Sunday night, added: “I cannot believe that this has happened again on the same line. We have to do something.”

An initial investigation into the Adamuz crash found a broken rail had caused one train to veer off the line into the path of an oncoming train.

Experts have called for more investment in maintenance in the wake of this year’s crashes.

Between 2018 and 2022, Spain spent an average of about $1.67bn each year on high-speed lines, more than other European countries with similar networks. However, only 16 percent of that was spent on maintenance or repairs, according to European Commission data; the rest was devoted to the infrastructure.

In contrast, Italy, Germany and France spent an average of between 33 and 39 percent of their budgets on maintenance, even though each has smaller networks than the 4,000km (2,485 miles) in Spain.

Experts call for investment in maintenance

Jose Maria Goicolea, spokesman for the Spanish Association of Civil Engineers, told Al Jazeera that with the increase in use of the rail network, “there has to be more spent on maintenance.

“In 1982, when there was the first line, it was a very small network. Now it is much bigger with much more usage. It is a whole new ball game now. The emphasis cannot be only on building new lines but doing more maintenance.”

About 40 million people used the high-speed rail trains in 2024, almost double the figure for 2019. In the first half of this year, about 25 million travelled on the high-speed network, a year-on-year fall of 14 percent.

The line between Madrid and Seville, where both crashes happened this year, is the only one in Spain using a German-made LZB control system dating from the 1970s, which is being phased out.

“I would close the line between Madrid and Seville while the LZB system is phased out. It was only partly responsible for Wednesday’s crash. It failed. But the other reason was human error, it seems,” Goicolea said. “However, this is up to the politicians, not me.”

He added that the crash in January was caused by faults in the line.

Ramiro Aupin Lopera, an expert in infrastructure who lectured at the University Politecnica de Catalunya, said that since 2011, in the wake of the financial crisis, there had been a “ridiculous” fall in investment in maintenance on the Spanish high-speed railway network.

“At the same time that there has been growing use of the network, there has been less investment in maintenance. It is no surprise that we have had two crashes in less than a year. It may come from ignorance or disdain towards science and infrastructure on the part of the politicians,” he told Al Jazeera.

Apart from the state-run Renfe, Spain has two private operators, Ouigo from France and Iryo, which is part of an Italian consortium. They have voiced concern over the LZB system.

Helen Venezuela, then director of Ouigo Espana, told Spanish radio Cadena Ser last year: “This line (Madrid-Seville) is equipped with an obsolete system like LZB. It is like watching Netflix in black and white. We are Netflix and the system is still in black and white.”

Diego Martin, of SEMAF, the Spanish train drivers’ union, said blaming rail workers for the latest disaster would not prevent future crashes.

“Blame does not prevent accidents; identifying and determining the causes does,” he said.

articles.title: Ex-Traitors players talk tactics and celebrity final predictions
articles.summary: Former contestants share their thoughts on life in the castle ahead of Friday's final.
articles.body:
Spoiler warning: This article reveals details from episode nine of The Celebrity Traitors, series two.

"Maya has played a damn good game", 61-year-old Judy Wilson says.

Judy, from Doncaster, took home the unwanted title of the first player to be banished from the castle in series four.

She told the BBC while it was a shame people didn't get to see more of her personality, she knew her daughter and fellow player, Roxy, would be "fighting for both of us".

"Roxy had warned me a few people were coming for me, and then my back got up... but I just tried to play the game.

"The thing is, they've got nothing to go off, so obviously people are all going to jump on the same bandwagon... I had to go down gracefully."

Roxy was adopted by Judy aged five, and said it was important for her and her mum to show viewers "if you're adopted or from an adverse background, you can still achieve things and be as regular as everyone else".

Roxy, 33, had been rooting for comedian and faithful Joanne McNally in the latest celebrity series, before she was banished by her fellow faithful on Thursday.

"She's wrong and strong, like me," Roxy jokes.

"When you're in there, your version of the truth becomes the truth, and nobody can tell you otherwise. You're in your own echo chamber."

Roxy said the game was "super intense, more intense than I expected".

After surviving for 11 episodes she was evenutally murdered by the traitors, though said she could see it coming.

"After being there for some time, you just expect it more and more every night. You're just kind of waiting."

Roxy had her own memorable moment on the show, when she clashed with crime writer and former barrister, Harriet Tyce, whose sights were – correctly – set on traitor Rachel Duffy.

Tyce voiced her theory at breakfast, but turned her frustrations to Roxy, who felt Tyce had interrupted Duffy when defending herself.

It was then Tyce produced the now-iconic line: "The benefit is to set the cat amongst the pigeons, Roxy."

"That moment itself I think has gone down in TV history, so I'm glad to be a part of it," Roxy laughs.

Leeds-born Theo Mayne has only watched clips of the latest series, but said, judging by those, he thinks Maya "will go all the way".

Mayne, 31, played the role of a faithful in the first ever UK series in 2022. Little was known about the show when it first graced our screens, but it has since exploded in popularity.

"I had no expectations – it just taught me to expect the unexpected," he said.

Mayne feels viewers "don't realise how hard the game is", with players' minds constantly in overdrive.

"It's hard to use your brain because you're just always thinking about, am I going to be murdered? Who is a traitor? Who is a faithful?

"There are so many different moving parts and the game is like a big turning cog."

He added: "You're always thinking, right, I need to survive the day, I need to look good, I need to not say this, I need to not do that... But I just went in there, was myself 100%... I mean, I told a few lies, but that's it!"

Mayne told the BBC he would do the show again in a heartbeat - and largely puts its success down to the first ever cast.

"I think if it wasn't for our guinea pig cast, it wouldn't be as big as it is."

Like her fellow veteran players, Jessie Roux, from Hull, is "rooting" for Maya.

Roux was - and always was - a faithful during her time on series four, until she was eliminated.

"It's hard because all of us aren't going off much, it's just trying to pick at random bits... as hard as it is, it's good vibes, even though it's stressful."

She added: "All of us got on and just hit it off, but when all of us had our different rules, the air just went cold.

"It was like, oh, all of us are in this now, and it did hit me then... I was just so on edge about being murdered."

A Traitors superfan, the 30-year-old was known not only for her bright make-up and outfits, but also for speaking openly about her stammer.

"I didn't have expectations because every game is a different game and I just wanted to do my best, but I guess my aim was to raise awareness of stammering.

"I had people reach out about how I'd helped them, I had mums reach out about their kids and how it's helped them... it was just good to educate others."

Series three's Alex Oleksy originally hails from Scotland, but lives in Whitby.

Although he admits the traitors are "playing it really well" this season, Oleksy is a true faithful and hopes they can defeat the traitors.

"James Acaster is such a reluctant traitor! We've seen all different kinds of traitors, but I don't think we've seen one that played quite like James."

Oleksy, 32, watched the show with his mother-in-law before signing up, and expected to "breeze right through it and win the money".

"I don't think I expected it to be quite so mentally taxing... it turns you so paranoid, it's unreal," he said.

"Everything is heightened; you're making friendships in the blink of an eye, you're deciding who your allies are...everything is just so heightened.

"It's like having a pot on the boil and as soon as these factors come into play, you're just constantly bubbling over."

He does caveat that by saying how much he loved being part of the show and how much it "taught him" about himself.

Oleksy was eventually banished by his fellow players, and says by that point, he was "desperate for a moment of vindication".

"I couldn't wait to get up there and be like, 'haha, told you'."

The final of Celebrity Traitors will air on BBC One at 20:00 GMT, and while many people will be glued to their sofas, venues across the region are hosting dedicated watch parties.

Headrow House, in Leeds, is hosting a screening of the final, as well as a repeat of the semi-final for those who missed it on Thursday, from 18:00.

The event is ticketed but free to attend.

Two Thirds Beer Co, in Sheffield, is also showing the final.

Owner, Ben Stubbs, said: "We're all huge fans of The Traitors here, and we actually showed the final of the last series earlier this year.

"We weren't quite sure what to expect, but the response was brilliant."

articles.title: Australian court rejects ‘mushroom murderer’ Erin Patterson’s appeal
articles.summary: Court rules Patterson will spend the rest of her life behind bars after denying parole.
articles.body:
An Australian court has dismissed an appeal by “mushroom murderer” Erin Patterson against her conviction and ruled that she should spend the rest of her life behind bars.

A three-judge panel at the Supreme Court of Victoria delivered its ruling on Friday. The justices said that Patterson, who was convicted last year of murdering three of her estranged husband’s ⁠relatives with a meal ⁠laced with deadly mushrooms, should not have the chance of parole.

“This offending was extraordinarily cold and calculated, and stands to be ⁠denounced in the strongest terms,” Justice Stephen McLeish, speaking on behalf ⁠of the panel, told the Melbourne court.

“In all the circumstances, after anxious consideration, we have concluded that the case involved such shocking criminality that it is inappropriate ⁠to fix a non-parole period.”

Patterson, then 51, was ⁠ convicted for the murder of her mother-in-law and father-in-law, Gail and Donald Patterson, and Gail’s sister, Heather Wilkinson, by serving them a lunch of beef wellington laced with death cap mushrooms.

She was also convicted of the attempted ‌murder of Ian Wilkinson, Heather’s husband, who survived the meal.

Her crimes involved an “elaborate series of deceptions” including falsely claiming a cancer diagnosis to explain the absence of her two children from the lunch, the judge noted.

The survivor testified that Patterson had told her guests she wanted their advice about what to tell the children about her diagnosis.

Patterson was sentenced to ⁠life in prison with a 33-year non-parole period, among the longest terms ever handed to a woman in Australia. She has always denied wrongdoing, saying the deaths were accidental.

Her lawyers had argued that certain evidence should have been kept from the trial, that her cross-examination ‌was unfair, and that placing the jury in the same hotel as other parties to the case compromised the result. Judges found these grounds for an appeal to be insufficient.

She can apply to Australia’s High Court to overturn the verdicts on her sentence and her convictions. The High Court is her last appeal option.

Patterson is only the second woman in Australia to be imprisoned for life without possibility of parole. The first is meatworker Katherine Knight, who was sentenced in New South Wales state in 2001 for the murder a year earlier of her partner John Price, whom she’d stabbed at least 37 times.

articles.title: How video game remakes tap the power of nostalgia
articles.summary: Video games are good at triggering nostalgia, a key reason why classic games keep getting remade.
articles.body:
The moment she saw footage from the remake of The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time, Kacey Doran picked up her phone. She had to tell her sister.

"Have you seen this?" messaged Doran, excitedly.

Nearly 30 years ago, a 10-year-old Doran had sat in front of her family's TV, reading out the dialogue on screen to her sister, a year younger, as they inched their way through the original Nintendo 64 game's sprawling, puzzle-filled dungeons. Ocarina's fantasy-like story, and beautiful music, enthralled them both.

It was also the first game Doran ever completed. Now, countless memories rushed back to her as she devoured clips of the fully redesigned version, due to arrive on the Switch 2 later this year.

Doran's sister messaged back: "I'm not tearing up… YOU'RE tearing up."

This is the power of nostalgia – and a perfect example of how video games can trigger it. Doran now teaches an esports course at Rowan University in New Jersey. She says the original Ocarina of Time, released in 1998, had a "magical" quality that she hopes to rediscover, and also share with her sister's children.

The video games industry has long leaned on remakes. From Mario Kart to the Final Fantasy series, or even Pac-Man, some games just keep coming back in updated forms, as new generations of gamers emerge and as computer hardware improves, enabling more detailed graphics and increasingly expansive game worlds.

While the emotional hook may be the most significant draw, putting out a remake can be a double-edged sword. Some gamers are very protective of their favourite titles and new versions don't always meet certain fans' astronomically high expectations.

Nostalgia is an important but mixed emotion, says Tim Wulf, at the Centre for Advanced Internet Studies in Bochum, Germany. It has positive aspects but also a kind of sadness, too. Happiness in remembering things that were important to us, and also an awareness that that time is now gone.

"It's a social emotion because memories that induce nostalgia for us are connected to other people," he explains, adding that nostalgia can boost our self-esteem while highlighting key social bonds.

Video games, says Wulf, are notoriously good at triggering nostalgia because gamers can "jump into the same environment". In other words, games are like time machines for our emotions, and returning to fondly remembered places can feel stabilising or reassuring in an ever-changing world.

Doran, for one, notes that when you return to a favourite old game, there's something satisfying about deploying previously learned skills. You know what to do here, you're winning again. Just like the old days.

Putting out remasters and remakes has been a "really successful" strategy for the games industry, says Piers Harding-Rolls, head of games research at Ampere Analysis.

"Tying in with established audiences and building on existing content is quite a safe route for a lot of companies," he adds. In many cases, it is cheaper to update an existing game rather than create a new title from scratch.

Among other remakes that have found big audiences recently are those of Resident Evil 4 and Assassin's Creed Black Flag.

But Ocarina of Time perhaps stands out because, ever since its original release, it has been considered by many as one of the greatest games ever made. "The interest from all the Gen Zs that I work with is really high," says Harding-Rolls. The legend of The Legend of Zelda, as it were.

Clearly, nostalgia is not the only driver of interest in the remake, and today's audiences will expect a game that plays to today's standards.

Games companies must keep innovating when linking contemporary audiences to the past, says Wulf, in order satisfy their desire for fresh experiences. And although Wulf himself was a big fan of the original, he has no personal interest in the Ocarina of Time remake. "I want a new game – I don't want to play an old game," he says. Nostalgia isn't always enough for some.

Plus, critics often highlight a tension between originals and remakes. Which is the definitive version? In 2021, Square Enix released the bizarrely titled Nier Replicant ver.1.22474487139... – a remaster of a game first published in 2010. One reviewer wrote , "What we're left with is two nearly identical Niers each vying to be the true Nier."

Fans may react badly should a remaster or remake fail to do justice to the source material. And, in the gaming world, angry fan reactions can be serious .

"There's always going to be that fan base or group of people that are going to nit-pick," says Stephanie Ijoma, chief executive and founder of NNESAGA, a consultancy and creative agency.

Ultimately, games developers working on remakes have to "find the right balance" between appealing to fans and allowing themselves to be creative with the material, she adds. "You can't make art in fear, you can't create in fear."

Ijoma gives the example of Final Fantasy VII. First released in 1997, it got a highly anticipated remake in 2020.

This was a game Ijoma played back in the late 1990s and she was thrilled to be able to share it with younger players today.

Remakes enable this sharing of experiences because getting old computer hardware or video games consoles to work, while a pastime loved by some , is not possible for everyone.

"I've tried multiple times to play Silent Hill 2 because I'm interested in older games but it's such a difficult game to come into nowadays," says Niklas Hallin, a solo indie game developer who runs the studio Neckbolt. "They made a remake and it's so smooth, it just works. It works on your modern hardware."

Hallin did not play many games as a child so he says nostalgia isn't much of a motivator for him. However, in his own games, he likes to include subtle stylistic references to classic games because he knows that this appeals to gamers.

Indie developers often lean on retro games aesthetics not just because people respond well to them – but also because they are easier to achieve. "You can't compete with billion dollar budgets, super high-fidelity, Triple A graphics," he says.

One question remains. The visual difference, today, between games released years apart is, arguably, negligible. So will there be any point in remaking a game from 2026 in, say, 2038? Will technology have moved on so much by then that it's actually worth it?

Harding-Rolls predicts that games companies will still seek to connect new audiences with classic titles by offering updates.

Remakes might become less about graphical improvements and more about editorial adjustments. "Reinterpretations," he says. "Or versions with additional content."

articles.title: ‘My life is buried here’: Iranian man whose 12 family members were killed
articles.summary: Hamed Mirzaei lost his wife, parents and many others in a devastating US-Israeli attack on Tehran.
articles.body:
Hamed Mirzaei lost 12 members of his family in an attack on a residential building in Tehran. Among those killed was his wife, 26-year-old Mohadeseh. The young couple had been planning to start a family.

He describes how the United States-Israeli attack on his home on March 9, 2026, changed his life in this first-person account, shared with Al Jazeera:

“Seven months have passed since the bombing. Even now, on many days, when I come to my senses, I find myself back at my destroyed home, searching for my loved ones.

“My grandfather and my father’s uncle built the house that was hit. They divided its apartments among their children. A year ago, when I got married, my wife and I moved into one of the apartments in the same building. We were just beginning to prepare for a child. We were young, with our whole lives ahead of us. Then the bombing happened.

“March 9 was a Monday. At about 1:00 in the afternoon, I left home to check in at work. At 2:30 pm, my wife messaged me, asking me to buy her some headache medicine on my way back. I called her to ask which medicine she wanted, but her phone was busy. We were expecting guests at home, so I called our guest’s phone. That line was busy, too. I hung up, intending to call my wife again.

“I was five minutes from home when I suddenly heard a whistling sound. The first missile had just struck.

“The ground shook beneath my feet from the force of the explosion. With my phone still in my hand, I called my wife again, but her phone was unreachable. I began calling my family members, my grandfather, my father, my mother. All their phones were unreachable.

“Even so, I thought our home had not been hit. I kept telling myself it was impossible that they had struck our house. I thought perhaps a missile had hit somewhere else in our neighbourhood. In those moments, all I wanted was to get home and see that the house was still standing.

“In those same minutes, five more missiles struck our home.

“When I arrived, I saw that everyone in the neighbourhood had come out of their homes, but I still couldn’t bring myself to step into the street. It never even crossed my mind that those missiles could have hit our house. But they had. Even from a distance, it was clear that all that remained of the house was its skeleton.

“When I reached it, everything was burning. All I could think about was getting to the second floor and finding my wife, but the staircase was gone. Several neighbours from the first floor were trapped beneath the rubble. The Red Crescent helped rescue them.

“I thought that if they kept searching, perhaps they would find my family alive somewhere beneath the debris, too. But they didn’t. No one was found that hour. Nor in the hours that followed. By nightfall, no one else had been found in the building. Twelve members of my family were missing, and I still couldn’t bring myself to leave.

“That night, the next day, the day after that, and every day following the attack, I returned to my home. For 20 days, I searched through the rubble and the remnants of the missiles and explosions for my loved ones. There was nothing left.

“My wife was killed. My sister-in-law, who had been a guest in our home, was killed. My father and mother, my grandfather and grandmother, my aunt’s husband and her daughter, my uncle, my father’s cousin, his wife and their child were all killed. Twelve members of my family died in the attack, and people ask me how I am.

“I miss them. I miss them more with every passing day. At first, I thought that perhaps, with time, our grief would ease and we would find some peace. But we haven’t. As each day passes, I feel worse.

“I was an only child, and I always thought that, although I had no brothers or sisters, I had a large family with whom I would grow old. All my life, the members of our extended family had lived together, side by side. Now all those people, and all the love that flowed through our family, have vanished.

“I am the only one left. There is no one else from my family. I am utterly alone.

“I am living proof for anyone who still believes that war can lead to a good outcome. Anyone who thinks war is good should look at what has happened to me and ask themselves: ‘What, in any of this, is good?’

“The building where I was born, the building where my father was born, the building where I had hoped my child would be born, all of it was destroyed in a fraction of a second. My home and my family were wiped out together. And when I miss them, I truly don’t know where to turn or what to look at.

“Seven months have passed since the day they destroyed our home, and every day, when I wake up, I come here to look at the ruins. I cannot bring myself to leave this place. I feel as though my life is buried here, and I return every day, hoping I might find some piece of it. But there is nothing left.

“When someone asks me what I am thinking or how I feel, I cannot answer. Everything I have ever done in my life was for the happiness of my family. Now I no longer have a family for whom I can do anything.

“Every day, I ask myself: ‘Why do I keep going?’ I have no answer.

“The difference between me and my family, who were killed, is that they were buried beneath the rubble, while I am still walking around. Other than that, I am just as dead as they are. The only difference is that my name is not included among the dead.”

articles.title: 3 killed in helicopter collision that shut down part of an Oregon highway
articles.summary: Two helicopters collided and crashed into a farm field Thursday near a small airport southwest of Portland, Oregon, killing all three people on board and forcing the closure of a key highway, authorities said.
articles.body: Two helicopters collided and crashed into a farm field Thursday near a small airport southwest of Portland, Oregon, killing all three people on board and forcing the closure of a key highway, authorities said. The crash killed 38-year-old Tyler Sturdevant, a pilot from Oregon, 22-year-old Maddie Aasbo, a flight instructor from Texas, and a student pilot from the United Kingdom, whose name has not been released, Yamhill County Sheriff Sam Elliott said during a news conference. Aasbo and the U.K. student pilot were on one aircraft, while Sturdevant was on the other, according to the sheriff’s office. Emergency crews responded around 2:15 p.m. following reports of a crash a few miles east of the McMinnville Airport, according to the sheriff’s office. By Thursday evening, officials were still working on their recovery efforts. Photos posted by the sheriff’s department show a green helicopter smashed upside down in a field, while a red helicopter lies crumpled and in pieces. One of the aircraft came from the aviation school Jerry Trimble Helicopters, which is located at the airport. “Our hearts and thoughts are with the individuals involved, their families, and everyone affected by this event,” the school said in a statement posted on social media. The school, which offers everything from demo flights for first-time flyers to advanced training, said it is cooperating with authorities to secure the site and determine the cause of the collision. Last year, the school posted a photo of Aasbo standing with another person in front of a helicopter and described her as a new private pilot going into instrument training. “These two are on to great things!” the post said. The Federal Aviation Administration said the collision was between a Robinson R22, a two-seat aircraft, and an Airbus H125, which can carry up to six passengers depending on the configuration. The FAA and National Transportation Safety Board are investigating. The Oregon Department of Transportation said Highway 233 is closed 1 mile (1.6 kilometers) west of Dayton because of the crash. There was no estimate for reopening. Local roads were also closed. The sheriff’s office urged the public to stay clear of the area. McMinnville, about 35 miles (56 kilometers) southwest of Portland, is home to about 34,000 people. The small airport situated on 650 acres (263 hectares) has two paved runways and remained open Thursday, according to its website. It’s partially bordered by homes and near the North American Aerospace Museum.
